doc.title: George Masso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997

title: Choosing work and jazz parties
summary: Masso now picks his gigs; Dick Gibson started jazz parties and the Jerome party is praised.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Right now in your career, do you pick and choose what you want to do a little more than before?
Yes. I’m happy to say I do. But there isn’t a lot to refuse you know? I mean most of the calls that I get, and almost everybody in this business is dealing over the telephone, you
know you get calls and you’re invited to various festivals or you’re invited to join a tour. But most of them are calls that I’m happy to receive and accept.
These jazz parties are an interesting little phenomenon in the country and I hope they continue.

I do too. It’s a nice concept. I think Dick Gibson started this years ago in Colorado, and a lot of other jazz societies around the country decided that they would take a weekend and call it either a jazz festival or a jazz party. And incidentally, this one here at the Jerome is just superb. It starts with a party and ends with a party.
